documents.title: Cache loss does not lose data
documents.text: The RAM and SSD caches are disposable acceleration. Acknowledged writes remain in object storage; losing the local cache makes queries cold again without losing committed data.

documents.title: Warm searches avoid remote reads
documents.text: The server warms its local SSD block cache in the background. Queries can read selected vector blocks from RAM or SSD instead of downloading them from object storage.

documents.title: The bucket is authoritative
documents.text: Glider acknowledges a write after publishing a complete immutable log object. Roots and logs define the committed state; local caches are derived and never replace durable storage.

documents.title: Recover after a restart
documents.text: A restarted server takes over the collection, fences its previous writer and replays the durable log. It serves every acknowledged write after recovery.

documents.title: Immutable vector packs
documents.text: Full vectors live in immutable object-store packs. In memory, the segmented engine retains the latest-ID directory, routing sketches and the unsealed log tail.

documents.title: Authenticate cached blocks
documents.text: Block bytes from RAM, SSD and object storage are authenticated against the committed block digest before decoding and scoring. Corrupt cached entries cannot become authoritative data.

documents.title: Filter by metadata
documents.text: Search supports equality, set membership, existence, numeric comparisons and logical combinations over string metadata. The full predicate is checked against the records read for the query.

documents.title: Get complete filtered results
documents.text: Add exact: true to search all live points and evaluate the full metadata filter exhaustively. The query returns up to k matches; bounded approximate search can miss eligible points.

documents.title: Combine numeric and category filters
documents.text: A filter can combine a color equality with a price range and tag membership. Conditions on the same key and different members of one filter object are ANDed.

documents.title: Route declared filter keys
documents.text: Required equality predicates on declared routed metadata keys restrict candidate routing. Glider still applies the complete filter to authenticated records during reranking.

documents.title: Choose your distance metric
documents.text: A collection has a fixed dimension and a fixed metric: squared Euclidean, Manhattan or cosine. Cosine vectors and queries must have nonzero norm and are normalized by the engine.

documents.title: Exact search is the recall oracle
documents.text: Exact search scores every live matching vector and sorts by distance then ID. Approximate query results are evaluated against exact neighbors using recall at k.

documents.title: Queries and writes run together
documents.text: Reader threads search immutable published views while the committer accepts writes. Each query observes a consistent snapshot; readers do not wait behind a long object-store write.

documents.title: Read your acknowledged writes
documents.text: A query sent after a successful write acknowledgement observes that write. A snapshot never exposes a partially applied write group or a partially published root.

documents.title: New writes are searchable immediately
documents.text: Recent acknowledged writes stay in the in-memory log tail until sealing. Selective queries scan that tail exactly and merge it with neighbors reranked from selected immutable blocks.

documents.title: Retry without applying a write twice
documents.text: Each write carries a request ID. Resending a retained request returns its original outcome instead of applying its mutations again. The retry window is bounded.

documents.title: Bound concurrent work
documents.text: Admission limits count queued and active operations and their encoded payload bytes. Requests that exceed available capacity return overload instead of creating an unbounded queue.

documents.title: One committer owns each collection
documents.text: Glider establishes single-writer ownership of each collection. A takeover fences earlier writers, while queries can execute concurrently on published snapshots.

documents.title: Start Glider with Docker
documents.text: Run the Glider server on port 8080 with a mounted Docker volume to preserve local data. Then write points with curl and issue your first vector query.

documents.title: Use the Python client
documents.text: The dependency-free Python client creates collections, upserts vectors and metadata, and returns nearest neighbors. Each collection selects its dimensions and distance metric.

documents.title: Browse collections in the console
documents.text: Open localhost:8080/console to browse your collections and points, run queries, and inspect the Glider server from your browser.

documents.title: Run on S3 or MinIO
documents.text: Glider supports S3-compatible object storage. Configure a bucket and a nonoverlapping namespace prefix; the service must provide strongly consistent reads and conditional object creation.

documents.title: Give agents durable memory
documents.text: The glider-mcp client exposes remember, recall and forget tools to MCP clients. Memories survive restarts and request IDs support safe retries within the retained window.

documents.title: Inspect query I/O
documents.text: Set profile: true on a query to include its execution mode, elapsed time, queue wait and remote I/O counters. These counters describe the reads caused by that query.
